methodology_overview: A-Mab applies a lifecycle of iterative risk assessments (Risk Assessments #1-#4, Figures 1.2/6.2, p236-238). RA#1-#2 (early) use prior knowledge and early development experience to prioritize process steps/parameters for characterization; RA#3 uses process-characterization (DoE/univariate, scale-down models) results to define draft design space and control strategy per unit operation; RA#4 uses full-scale/commercial and prior mAb knowledge to finalize CPP selection and the control strategy. Two DISTINCT criticality assessments must be separated: (1) CQA (quality-attribute) criticality (Chapter 2), scored on TWO dimensions only - Tool #1: Criticality (Risk Score) = Impact x Uncertainty; Tool #2: Criticality (RPN) = Severity x Likelihood - explicitly NOT including manufacturing capability or detectability; this yields a 'continuum of criticality' (not binary critical/non-critical). (2) PROCESS-PARAMETER criticality / control-strategy risk, which DOES use a full three-axis FMEA. Two variants appear: (a) Drug Product process parameters (Section 5.3.3.3-5, p206-214): an initial Risk Ranking & Filtering (RRF) screen scores Severity = Main-effect impact x Interaction-effect impact to decide study type (Table 5.16: Severity >=32 multivariate; 8-16 multivariate or justified univariate; 4 univariate; <=2 no study; main-effect scores Table 5.17: No Impact 2 / Minor 4 / Major 8), then POST-characterization an FMEA (Table 5.21) computes RPN = Severity x Occurrence x Detection to designate CPP/WC-CPP. (b) Overall CQA control-strategy FMEA (Chapter 6, Figure 6.1, Table 6.1/6.2): RPN = S x O x D where S = CQA Criticality Level (from Tool #1), O = process capability (probability CQA exceeds acceptable range), D = testing/detectability; the process-capability RPN is rescaled to a 1-10 occurrence score. Process parameters are finally categorized by the decision logic of Figures 6.3/6.4: does parameter variability significantly impact CQAs? If yes -> CPP (high risk of falling outside design space) or WC-CPP (low risk); if no but it impacts process performance/consistency -> KPP (high risk) or GPP (low risk). Criticality is treated as a continuum, and control-strategy mitigations can move a CPP to WC-CPP.
criticality_or_rpn_rule: POST-characterization Drug Product FMEA (Table 5.25, p214): RPN = Severity x Occurrence x Detection. CPP threshold: 'Severity >= 8 OR RPN > 72 (High Risk) = parameter is a CPP.' 'RPN > 48 and <= 72 (Medium risk) and severity < 8 = further analyzed for CPP designation (historical/literature review, compare control range vs acceptable range; corrective action to reduce occurrence/improve detection).' 'RPN <= 48 (Low risk) and severity < 8 = not a CPP.' (Page 212 restates: 'Process parameters that have severity >= 8 or RPN > 72 are classified as CPPs.') Initial RRF screen (Table 5.16, p206): Severity = Main effect x Interaction effect determines study type (>=32 multivariate; 8-16 multivariate or justified univariate; 4 univariate; <=2 no study). Chapter-6 process-capability RPN (Table 6.2, p242): RPN=SxOxD, >=100 High risk of QA failure (Low capability, occurrence score 10); 31-90 Medium (score 3); <=30 Low risk (High capability, score 1). CQA criticality (Chapter 2) is separate: Impact x Uncertainty (Tool #1) or Severity x Likelihood/RPN (Tool #2), two axes only.

detection_scale.meaning: None - failure will not be detected with in-process or CofA testing (Table 5.24, p214)
Low - in-process testing/monitoring will not detect this failure, but CofA testing will catch it
Moderate - in-process testing/monitoring will not catch failure during the unit operation; detection delayed several downstream unit operations but prior to CofA testing
High - failure may or may not be detected by in-process controls/monitoring but would definitely be detected in the next downstream operation
Very High - failure can be immediately and readily detected by inspection, in-process testing or monitoring controls prior to downstream unit operation
D scored 1/3/10: 1 = can readily detect; 3 = indirect ability to detect; 10 = cannot readily detect

occurrence_scale.meaning: Very high - parameter failure occurs on the order of once every 100 units or greater (Table 5.23, p213)
High - parameter failure occurs on the order of once every 1000 units
Moderate - parameter failure occurs on the order of once every 2000 units
Low - parameter failure occurs on the order of once every 5000 units
Minimal - parameter failure occurs on the order of once every 10000 units or lower
O scored 1/3/10 by process capability: 1 = high capability/react, few WC-CPPs no CPPs; 3 = multiple WC-CPPs, no CPPs; 10 = influenced solely by CPPs

severity_scale.meaning: Very High - parameter deviation causes definite impact to product quality; lot(s) need to be rejected (Table 5.22, p213)

High - deviation will probably impact product quality; discrepancy initiated, product assessed after significant supplemental testing (may include accelerated stability) and/or significant re-processing required
Moderate - deviation potentially impacts product quality; product assessed after supplemental t=0 testing and/or minor re-processing required
Slight - deviation unlikely to impact product quality; no supplemental testing (memo may be issued to release lot) and no re-processing required
Low/None - deviation has no impact to product quality; no remediation/re-processing required
No Impact 2 (variation not detectable/within assay variability); Minor Impact 4 (within acceptable range); Major Impact 8 (outside acceptable range, can be near edge of failure)
S scored 1/3/10: 1 = will not lead to failure of DS/DP to meet quality targets; 3 = could lead to failure but other steps mitigate; 10 = will lead to failure, other steps cannot mitigate

definitions.CPP: Critical Process Parameter: a process parameter whose variability has an impact on a critical quality attribute and therefore should be monitored or controlled to ensure the process produces the desired quality (ICH Q8R2). A-Mab sub-divides by risk of falling outside the design space: a CPP has a HIGH risk of falling outside the design space; a Well-Controlled CPP (WC-CPP) has a LOW risk of falling outside the design space. Risk assessed from equipment design, process control capability/complexity, size/reliability of design space, ability to detect/measure a parameter deviation, etc. (p21, p240).
definitions.KPP: Key Process Parameter: an adjustable parameter that, when maintained within a narrow range, ensures optimum/operational process performance/reliability; does NOT meaningfully affect critical product quality attributes. Ranges set during development; changes managed in the quality system (p240, p275). In A-Mab logic a KPP results when a parameter does not significantly impact CQAs but is HIGH risk to process performance/consistency (vs GPP = low risk).
definitions.NOR: Normal Operating Range: a defined range, within the Proven Acceptable Range, specified in the manufacturing instructions as the target and range at which a process parameter is controlled while producing unit-operation material or final product meeting release criteria and CQAs (PQRI) (p274).
definitions.PAR: Proven Acceptable Range: a characterised range of a process parameter for which operation within this range, while keeping other parameters constant, will result in producing material meeting relevant quality criteria (ICH Q8R2) (p274). (Note: A-Mab primarily uses knowledge space / design space / control space terminology; 'Proven Acceptable Ranges' also appears p33.)
definitions.design_space: The multidimensional combination and interaction of input variables (e.g., material attributes) and process parameters demonstrated to provide assurance of quality. Working within the design space is not a change; movement out is a change requiring regulatory post-approval process (ICH Q8R2). In A-Mab the design space is a subset of the knowledge space known to give acceptable CQA values, and the process is normally run within a narrower control space that lies within the design space; design spaces represent multivariate interactions of CPPs/WC-CPPs and CQAs (p240-241, p273).
definitions.control_strategy: A planned set of controls, derived from current product and process understanding, that assures process performance and product quality; controls include parameters and attributes of DS/DP materials/components, facility/equipment operating conditions, in-process controls, finished-product specifications, and associated monitoring methods/frequency (ICH Q10). In A-Mab each CQA has an individual control strategy built from control elements (input material, procedural, process-parameter controls, in-process/release/characterization testing, process monitoring); the sum of individual strategies = overall control strategy (p236-237).

worked_examples.parameter: Pumping Speed - failure mode 'greater than maximum allowed speed' -> aggregation/splashing
worked_examples.outcome: RPN = 216 (also Detection = 6). Severity<8 but RPN>72 -> CPP; mitigated by control strategy (speed documented each fill accuracy check, acceptable operating range from design space) -> classified WC-CPP (Table 5.21, p212)

worked_examples.parameter: Stopper force - 'not fully seated' -> loss of seal integrity
worked_examples.outcome: RPN = 200 (Detection = 2). Severity>=8 -> CPP; raised-stopper detection + acceptable range from design space -> WC-CPP

worked_examples.parameter: Stopper placement - 'unstoppered vial exits filler' -> loss of seal integrity
worked_examples.outcome: RPN = 240 (Detection = 6). Severity>=8 -> CPP; stopper detection system + final vial inspection -> WC-CPP

worked_examples.parameter: Capping pressure - 'outside the validated range' -> critical defects (cracked vials)
worked_examples.outcome: RPN = 160 (Detection = 10). Severity>=8 -> CPP; trained operators/SOPs/settings recorded + acceptable range from design space -> WC-CPP
CPP - pH<3.2 may lead to aggregation, pH>4.0 not studied in clearance study (Table 4.18, p133)
WC-CPP - longer times lead to aggregation, shorter times may give incomplete inactivation
GPP - no effect seen on stability or inactivation
WC-CPP (text: 'WC-PP') - lower temperatures may give incomplete inactivation at short time and higher pH

worked_examples.parameter: Production Bioreactor step (vs seed expansion / harvest)
worked_examples.cqa: Aggregate, Deamidated isoforms, aFucosylation, CHO HCP, DNA
worked_examples.outcome: Production Bioreactor is the ONLY upstream step that impacts (forms) product-quality CQAs, so it is the only step used to define the upstream design space; seed steps low risk (no product accumulation); N-1 seed and harvest impact process attributes/titer (KPP) but not CQAs (p85-86)
